slides.title: Sleeping Machines
slides.subtitle: A trainable substrate for intelligence through time and sparse events.
slides.notes: Private review deck. The founder proposes a €3M raise. €50M priced pre-money is the central bullish negotiating thesis developed here; €100M is a stretch scenario, neither an independent fair-value appraisal nor an investor offer. The research evidence is exploratory and single-seed. No customer interest has been reported. No investor, vendor or customer has been contacted in preparing this deck.
slides.hero:
Build useful capacity faster than active computation.
From datacenters to mobile devices and robotics.

slides.title: A new model family. A new computing substrate.
slides.subtitle: The goal: useful intelligence with less active work, persistent state and adaptation.
slides.notes: Core mechanisms remain explicit: computational delays and temporal races; sparse addressed memory updates; small messages that mix input and persistent state; separate keys and values; credit to unrealized routes; silence-aware supervision where applicable. The newest language core implements a factorized temporal law, hard selection, deep local memories and route credit. It does not yet cover every general event-substrate mechanism. Future clockless hardware is a proposed implementation route, not a fabricated asset.

cards.label: CAPACITY BEYOND ACTIVITY
cards.body: Grow available learned state while selecting a small amount of computation for each event.

cards.label: TIME COMPUTES
cards.body: Message content, delays and local state determine which computation happens and when.

cards.label: CLOUD TO EMBODIMENT
cards.body: Pursue models and runtimes first; extend the same principles to edge systems and future clockless silicon.

slides.banner: The investment thesis is an architecture–runtime–hardware platform, with staged proof.

slides.title: The constraints reach from power grids to robot batteries.
slides.subtitle: Economic context for efficient intelligence; these figures are not our revenue market.
slides.notes: IEA projects all datacenter electricity, not only AI demand; GSMA subscribers are not annual device shipments; IFR reports industrial-robot installed stock, not all robotics. These denominators cannot be summed into a TAM. The thesis is an inference about potential demand for verified efficient computation. Incumbents are also improving rapidly, which raises the threshold for a commercially useful alternative.

cards.label: DATACENTERS
cards.body: TWh/year, 2025 → 2030 central IEA projection. Power and data movement make system efficiency economically important.

cards.label: MOBILE
cards.body: Unique mobile subscribers in GSMA’s 2026 report. On-device inference creates a prospective route to broad distribution.

cards.label: ROBOTICS
cards.body: Industrial robots operating in 2025. Sparse sensing, persistent state and adaptation are prospective use cases.

slides.banner: Select one measurable initial workload; expand only after quality and system gains hold.

slides.title: Hard sparse computation that can learn its alternatives.
slides.subtitle: Conceptual event path; the trained language core is implemented in a synchronous software emulator.
slides.notes: This construction combines familiar vector operations with temporal computation and sparse state. Separate keys determine addressing; values determine delivered content. Counterfactual credit gives unrealized alternatives a learning signal without softening the hard forward route. The present implementation is not a physical asynchronous machine: autograd, shared training windows, clipping and Adam remain. Winner-only inference still scores all candidate keys.

steps.label: 01 / MESSAGE
steps.body: Encode incoming signal. Content and persistent memory influence the emission delay.

steps.label: 02 / RACE
steps.body: Score candidate keys. A temporal race selects an addressed receiver.

steps.label: 03 / MEMORY
steps.body: Deliver the selected value and evolve local persistent state through deep layers.

steps.label: 04 / LEARNING
steps.body: Train contents and timings using selected and unrealized alternatives; charge the credit work.

slides.banner: Inference selects values sparsely; current training still computes losing alternatives.

slides.title: Three results make the architecture worth scaling.
slides.subtitle: Completed text8 experiments; all numbers remain exploratory single-seed evidence.
slides.notes: T256 test values come from completed held-out evaluations; training scores and pending 90M results are excluded. One nominal pass uses about 9.994M training positions. A single seed and differing native/control training order limit generalization. The p96 improvement over LSTM is only {best_lstm_gain:.4f} bpc, with {best_lstm_fit_ratio:.2f} times fitting work; it establishes a promising quality direction, not an iso-quality resource win.

cards.label: LANGUAGE QUALITY
cards.body: Best p96 / D4 result is slightly ahead of saved one-pass LSTM at {lstm_bpc:.3f}; it uses more work.

cards.label: CAUSAL MECHANISM ABLATION
cards.body: Adding value-based route credit improves the same p32 / D4 model with +{credit_fit_increase_pct:.2f}% estimated fitting work.

cards.label: CAPACITY / SELECTION
cards.body: Doubling the credited p32 memory pool improves quality while keeping selected writes per input position fixed.

slides.banner: Distinctive mechanisms affect learning; scale, modern controls and serving economics remain open.

slides.title: A promising quality–work frontier at small scale.
slides.subtitle: Same text8 held-out region and T256 windows; saved one-pass controls, not optimized frontier baselines.
slides.notes: p32 / D4 credited: {credit_bpc:.6f} bpc, 7.243 estimated whole-fit TFLOPs, 108,875 parameters. Saved Transformer-256×2: {transformer_bpc:.6f}, 111.262 TFLOPs, 1,658,907 parameters. This gives {transformer_fit_ratio:.2f}× lower fitting arithmetic and {transformer_parameter_ratio:.2f}× fewer parameters for this saved control, with {transformer_credit_gain:.4f} lower bpc. The strong one-pass LSTM is {lstm_bpc:.6f} at 20.306 TFLOPs. Best native p96 is {best_bpc:.6f} at 58.648 TFLOPs. A modern tuned Transformer/MoE/SSM and larger-data matched protocol are still needed.
slides.caveat: BPC ↓ is better. Fitting includes credit/backward/clip/Adam estimates; conventions and training order differ. One seed. No wall-time or energy claim.

slides.title: Learning the alternatives changes the result.
slides.subtitle: The same p32 / D4 model, data budget, seed and evaluation window.
slides.notes: The local linearized credit estimator adds a derivative pathway for alternative delivered values while preserving the forward winner. It is not the exact full counterfactual trajectory gradient. The paired p32 / D4 T256 gain is {credit_gain:.6f} bpc, with {credit_fit_increase_pct:.4f}% extra whole-fit estimated operations. The corresponding p32 / D8 gain is {depth_credit_gain:.6f}. Attribution is stronger than a comparison between different widths, but a single seed still leaves variance and hyperparameter sensitivity unresolved.
stats: Timing-only credit versus added local alternative-value route credit.
Hard forward selection and parameter count retained.
Derived from the BPC difference; one controlled seed.
slides.detail: Depth-8 also improves by {depth_credit_gain:.3f} bpc with route credit. This supports the credit mechanism across two depths; replication is next.
slides.banner: A falsifiable architectural mechanism, with a small counted arithmetic increment.

slides.title: More available state. The same eight selected writes.
slides.subtitle: Matched credited p32 / D4 pool expansion: 16 → 32 slots.
slides.notes: Pool 2 → 4 changes memory scalars from 512 to 1,024 and parameters from 108,875 to 177,019. At T256, quality changes from {credit_bpc:.6f} to {pool_bpc:.6f}. Selected writes remain eight per input position; candidate keys increase 16 → 32. Winner-only per-position arithmetic increases {pool_sparse_increase_pct:.4f}%, but whole-fit estimated work rises {pool_fit_increase_pct:.4f}%. All memory and key scoring still cost resources. A negative uncredited pool expansion was measured at D8, while this positive credited pair is D4; this is not a full matched 2×2 interaction test.
slides.banner: Quality improves by {pool_gain:.3f} bpc; total capacity and learning costs remain explicitly charged.

slides.title: The sparse path is implemented; system proof is next.
slides.subtitle: Traced arithmetic per input position. Only selected proposal values are computed in the winner path.
slides.notes: Small random float64 fixtures match full-emulator logits within roughly 1e-10. Actual trained float32 winner/state/cache parity and a full held-out rescore are prepared and pending. The prepared CPU worker retains prepacked matrices per fixed model version, but native admission remains unrun. Candidate key scans, copying, residency, setup, gather traffic, cache invalidation and quality must all be included in serving comparisons. The deck deliberately does not attach the trained quality to an unverified production backend or convert FLOPs to joules.
slides.caveat: These are backend/shape estimates. Native evaluation pays overlapping-window warmup (~2 positions/target); LSTM recurrent evaluation differs. Not a service-cost win.

slides.title: An adaptation signal exists. Its work is accounted for.
slides.subtitle: An earlier integrated CPU model, on a new development stream; separate from the latest language fits.
slides.notes: Frozen versus online evaluation scores 8,191 targets with predict-before-update, 16-character delayed-feedback blocks, lr 1e-4, fresh Adam, clipping and full-backbone gradients. Both arms retain persistent local state. BPC improves by {online_gain:.6f}; total processing-operation estimates increase from 210,902,697 to 2,264,163,359, a {online_work_ratio:.4f}× ratio. This supports trainability under adaptation, not inexpensive lifelong learning. Retention, drift, long-horizon memory and local asynchronous learning need new evidence. Loihi 2 already provides an on-chip learning precedent.
slides.banner: Online-learning upside: persistent adaptive systems. Current result: one costed pilot.

slides.title: The contribution is the complete construction.
slides.subtitle: Established alternatives already address parts of this problem; they remain essential controls.
slides.notes: The pitch does not assert sole invention of sparse activation, gating, normalization, key/value separation or hardware learning. It proposes an integrated trainable temporal substrate and evaluates consequences. The latest native language model has no dense carrier or n-gram count component, but remains a restricted software realization. A weak result in one restricted variant should be diagnosed; genuine superiority requires matched strong controls. Intel Loihi 2 is cited on the adaptation and strategic slides.

slides.title: Enter through software. Earn the hardware expansion.
slides.subtitle: Proposed commercialization sequence; no customers or partner interest yet.
slides.notes: The first commercial workload is a selection hypothesis rather than a confirmed customer request. A staged software route lowers dependency on new silicon and permits independent benchmarking. A clockless implementation could benefit from less global synchronization and local state, but clock precision, signal fanout, memory, interconnect and fabrication overhead may dominate. Hardware economic claims require measurements. Costs for an ASIC tapeout are not estimated or funded here.

cards.body: License a validated model/runtime for a chosen persistent sequence workload. Demonstrate quality and complete serving cost.

cards.label: 02 / ACCELERATOR CO-DESIGN
cards.body: Port verified kernels, profile memory and event execution, then pursue a joint platform or IP license.

cards.label: 03 / CLOCKLESS SUBSTRATE
cards.body: Explore delay precision, sparse local state and event scheduling in FPGA/ASIC feasibility work after software gates pass.

slides.title: Incumbents have reasons to evaluate a new substrate.
slides.subtitle: Potential counterparties only. Strategic relevance is an inference; no relationship is claimed.
slides.notes: AMD is the strongest identified public fit precedent, not a presumed buyer. Its Ventures page lists Series A–C focus, so a €3M research-stage round may need angels/specialist deep-tech leads before strategic institutional investment. Intel’s system is a research prototype; Google has substantial internal alternatives and could build rather than license. Possible routes are benchmark collaboration, co-development, licensing, investment or eventual acquisition; none is a current pipeline asset. No company logos or implied endorsements are used.

slides.title: Capture a fraction of verified value created.
slides.subtitle: Illustrative annual economics, contingent on quality and complete system savings.
slides.notes: Eligible spend is the subset of workload cost we can actually influence; it is not total hyperscaler capex or global electricity spend. Savings must be measured at equivalent quality, latency and service conditions. Capture share is a pricing assumption. €1B × 20% × 20% yields €40M annual license revenue, leaving €160M buyer benefit before transition overhead. 100M new devices × €0.50 is €50M device-cycle revenue, not subscriber-stock recurring ARR. A robotics illustration of one million paying systems at €50/year gives €50M/year, but assumes a large unsupported adoption level. These routes may overlap and should not be summed.

slides.title: Use capital to retire the decisive uncertainties.
slides.subtitle: Milestones are proposed gates, not completed deliverables or guaranteed dates.
slides.notes: The timing is a planning assumption measured from funding. Three seeds and tuned modern controls are validation targets, not present assets. The ≥20% complete-cost gate is a proposed commercial screen and should be adapted to actual service requirements before experiments. Model quality and resource accounting must stay jointly comparable. Current owner queues retain priority; no new training or unguarded compute is launched to prepare this deck. Continued funding depends on completed results, measurable economics and a credible next workload rather than predictions entered as benchmark evidence.

stages.label: MONTHS 0–3
stages.body: Hire initial team. Admit trained sparse parity, complete 90M evidence and three-seed comparisons. Resolve IP and data-room rights.

stages.label: MONTHS 3–6
stages.body: Benchmark latency, traffic, memory and joules on one chosen workload with tuned controls. Target ≥20% full-system cost reduction at matched quality.

stages.label: MONTHS 6–12
stages.body: Pursue independent reproduction and prospective design-partner trials. Validate willingness to pay and a deployable runtime.

stages.label: MONTHS 12–18
stages.body: Scale a winning workload; test drift/retention and a hardware feasibility path. Raise the next round only on stronger evidence.

slides.banner: If a gate fails, diagnose or narrow the wedge before increasing compute or committing to silicon.

slides.title: Quality and work, in the same units for every model.
slides.subtitle: Completed one-pass 10M text8 fits; T256 held-out evaluation; estimated operation counts.
slides.notes: All fitting columns include estimated complete step arithmetic rather than forward-only model FLOPs. Native representative operator traces include backward, alternative credit, clipping and Adam; dense controls use shape formulas with backward approximately twice forward. Inference includes traced unit and special-function arithmetic, but not DRAM traffic, copying, allocation, RNG, evaluation overhead or physical energy. Formula conventions differ and are stated. Per-position columns use one shared denominator type per column. Winner-only arithmetic is explicitly separated from emulator quality. Full CSV contains all 13 native fits and both controls.
slides.caveat: Fit MF/pos = per training position. Inference MF/pos = per evaluated input position. Native quality uses training evaluator; winner-only trained parity/rescore pending. Native overlap warmup adds work per scored target. Full 15-row CSV retains older models.

slides.title: The comparison boundaries are part of the evidence.
slides.subtitle: Maintain the original records and disclose what a result actually measures.
slides.notes: The native score pays overlap-window warmup, evaluating roughly twice as many input positions as scored targets at T256. LSTM recurrent evaluation is a different protocol. Native T256 coverage is 999,936 targets, while original saved controls have a slightly different tail. The raw difference is small but must be disclosed. The 90M owner campaign is active; checkpoints count presented targets, including repeated random segments, and do not establish a final 90M held-out result. No pending cells are filled with expectations. No additional Transformer or LSTM training is launched here; the user reserved it for AWS.

slides.title: Keep the failures beside the positive mechanism results.
slides.subtitle: A disciplined research program should revise interpretations when evidence changes.

Normalized read/write credit gives 2.3840 versus read-credit 2.3715; other write-credit variants diverge and are retained historically. Best p96 quality gains over LSTM with more work. DVS small screens suggested lower coarsening work, but the full all-seed quality gate failed and the strong RBF control remains better. Target-dependent E63/E79 mixtures are quarantined for leakage and never used in this deck.

At a €3B outcome and 10% retained equity, the required probabilities are much higher than at a €30B exit with 50% retention. A lower discount rate increases the present value, while delays and dilution reduce it. In the €3M/€50M round, an investor retains 1.6981% at exit if 30% of its initial stake survives, giving €{conditional_proceeds_m_eur:.2f}M or {conditional_moic:.2f}× gross MOIC in the assumed €10B success outcome. That conditional upside is not expected return; failure is zero and cash-flow timing/preferences are omitted.
slides.caveat: Sensitivity analysis, not observed probabilities. No preferred-stock waterfall, intermediate distributions, follow-on investment cash flows or option-pool adjustment modeled.
